question: Which of the following National Parks is located in Madhya Pradesh?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bandhavgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bandhavgarh National Park** is located in the Umaria district of Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• It was declared a national park in **1968** and later became a Tiger Reserve under Project Tiger in **1993**.
 
• The park is renowned for its **high density of Bengal Tigers** and is one of the best places in India for tiger sightings.
 
• Bandhavgarh is also home to other fauna such as leopards, deer species, and over 250 species of birds.
 
• The park has historical significance due to the presence of the **ancient Bandhavgarh Fort**, believed to be over 2,000 years old.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Parks in Madhya Pradesh:**

 
 
• Madhya Pradesh is often called the **"Tiger State"** of India due to its significant tiger population.
 
• Other famous national parks in Madhya Pradesh include **Kanha National Park, Satpura National Park, and Pench National Park**.
 
• These parks are known for their rich biodiversity and serve as major tourist attractions for wildlife enthusiasts.
 
 
 
• **Project Tiger:**
 
 
• A conservation initiative launched by the Government of India in **1973** to protect tigers and their habitats.
 
• Bandhavgarh is one of the reserves under this project aimed at increasing tiger populations in the country.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity of Bandhavgarh:**
 
 
• Bandhavgarh has a mix of deciduous forests, grasslands, and bamboo patches that support diverse flora and fauna.
 
• The park is home to species such as Sloth Bears, Indian Bison (Gaur), and several reptiles and amphibians.
 
 
 
• **Bandhavgarh Fort:**
 
 
• An ancient fort located within the park, believed to have been gifted by Lord Rama to his brother Lakshmana, as per Hindu mythology.
 
• The fort offers panoramic views of the surrounding forests and is of archaeological importance.
